semantic_contracts.current_semantics: Twelve public fields retain the incumbent concrete UTC datetime type and their containing structs retain serde derives.

Three root public fields are optional. Because their serde fields have no skip_serializing_if attribute, None serializes as an explicit JSON null rather than an omitted key or epoch sentinel; Serde deserialization maps both explicit null and a missing Option field to None.
Feature-gated workflow code directly acquires ambient UTC now for create, update, retention, and verification records.

CI publish writes null on retention parse failure, but defaults failed standard-duration conversion to zero and writes expiry equal to acquisition time. CI clean and list disable their age/recent cutoffs on parse or conversion failure and may include every otherwise-matching row. Archive retention parse or conversion failure writes expires_at as JSON null.
Generic serde JSON pretty serialization writes directly and generic serde JSON deserialization reads the entire file.
Both public serde types acquire ambient UTC now; the report is returned to callers and no in-tree BenchmarkReport file writer was found.

semantic_contracts.surface: PostgreSQL binary DATE and TIMESTAMP tests
semantic_contracts.current_semantics: Production DATE, TIMESTAMP, and INTERVAL decoding is owned. Chrono independently constructs expected DATE and TIMESTAMP text only; the INTERVAL expected value calls the same owned render_interval_text helper and is not an independent Chrono oracle.

semantic_contracts.surface: Chrono-generated String fields in root and excluded conformance reports
semantic_contracts.current_semantics: Twelve public timestamp fields are generated with Chrono. The first seven root-member report types derive Serialize only. The four wired RaptorQ models and excluded PING report also derive Deserialize, where timestamps remain unvalidated String values. Wired ConformanceHistory accepts arbitrary JSON strings and records_since compares ConformanceRecord.timestamp lexicographically rather than as parsed instants.
Direct chrono calls are inside the module test region; no production Redis chrono call was found.
The prior foundation owns render-only nonnegative Unix nanoseconds and the CLI call; it does not own parsing, offsets, negative instants, serde, or public chrono fields.

semantic_contracts.surface: Agent Mail reservation and evidence timestamps
semantic_contracts.current_semantics: A private owned parser accepts trimmed date-time text with T, Z or signed HH:MM offsets, truncates fractional seconds, accepts second 60, rejects negative Unix results, and returns Option<SystemTime>. Its civil-date validation is structural rather than a full RFC3339/calendar proof.
semantic_contracts.accepted_syntax: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS followed optionally by a first dot and any unvalidated suffix, then Z or a signed HH:MM offset; everything after the first dot in the seconds component is discarded.
semantic_contracts.calendar_validation: Month and day are independently bounded to 1..12 and 1..31; invalid month/day combinations can normalize through civil conversion.

semantic_contracts.surface: UTC foundation, ATP logging, and JetStream
semantic_contracts.current_semantics: Three owned emitters exist with distinct input and precision policies: nonnegative Unix nanoseconds with trimmed fractions, SystemTime seconds with pre-epoch clamped to zero, and signed SystemTime with exactly nine fractional digits.
Scheduling, monotone, virtual, and logical time stay separate from UTC calendar semantics.

semantic_contracts.surface: SystemTime, logical Time, epoch-millisecond integers, and Duration/TTL values
semantic_contracts.current_semantics: ATP grants and backup metadata use SystemTime, offline tuning uses logical Time or Debug SystemTime text, Kafka records use Option<i64> epoch milliseconds, and Redis TTL behavior uses Duration. These are distinct temporal schemas, not Chrono or external-time migration substitutes.
